sections.title: The problem attention solves

paragraphs.text: A language model reads one token at a time. When it sees the word bank, it cannot know yet whether the next word will be river or account, and it cannot know whether bank was meant as money at all. Every earlier token stays available to the model, but the model has to decide which of them matter for the token it is about to write.
paragraphs.explainArabic: الموديل يقرأ رمزًا واحدًا في كل مرة. عند رؤية كلمة bank لا يعرف بعد إن كان 다음ها river أم account.attention هي آلية اختيار أي الكلمات السابقة تهم للرمز الحالي.

paragraphs.text: Attention is the mechanism that decides. For every token, the model computes a score against every earlier token, turns those scores into weights, and uses the weights to build a richer representation of the current token before predicting the next one.
paragraphs.explainArabic: attention تحسب درجة لكل كلمة سابقة، تحوّل الدرجات إلى أوزان، ثم تبني تمثيلًا أغنى للرمز الحالي قبل التنبؤ بالكلمة التالية.

paragraphs.text: Three things happen inside one attention step:
items: Score: compare the current token against every earlier token.
Weight: turn those scores into numbers that sum to one.
Mix: blend the earlier tokens into the current representation by those weights.

paragraphs.text: A weight of 0.4 does not mean 40 percent of the answer. It means the current token borrows 40 percent of that earlier token's contribution when it forms its own representation. The same weights are then reused by every later mechanism that needs to know what mattered.
paragraphs.explainArabic: الوزن 0.4 لا يعني 40% من الإجابة، بل أن الرمز الحالي يستعير 40% من مساهمة تلك الكلمة السابقة عند بناء تمثيله.

keySentences: Attention is the mechanism that decides.
A weight of 0.4 does not mean 40 percent of the answer.
takeaways: Weights are borrow shares, not answer shares.
Every token does this against every earlier token.

studyAid.whyItMatters: Retrieval quality in a RAG system is the same question asked of a model: which earlier parts of the input deserve weight.

confusion.simpleEnglish: The model looks at everything it has read and gives the important words a bigger vote.
confusion.simpleArabic: الموديل يقرأ كل ما سبق، ويعطي الكلمات المهمة صوتًا أكبر.
confusion.analogy: A meeting where each participant speaks, but the chair only listens closely to the two people whose answer matters.

prediction.question: If every token attends to every earlier token, what grows fastest as the input gets longer?
prediction.answer: The number of score computations, which grows quadratically. A context of length n needs about n squared comparisons.

sections.title: Why the cost matters

paragraphs.text: Quadratic attention is the reason long-context work is expensive. Doubling the input does not double the bill, it quadruples the attention part of it. This is why chunking, retrieval, and caching exist as separate disciplines instead of being solved by making the window bigger.
paragraphs.explainArabic: الانتباه الرباعي هو سبب كلفة السياقات الطويلة: مضاعفة الإدخال تربّع الكلفة. لهذا يوجد chunking و retrieval و caching كحقول منفصلة.

paragraphs.text: Compare the attention work for two context lengths.
That function is arithmetic, not a benchmark. It tells you the shape of the curve and nothing about how fast your hardware runs it. Real numbers come from measuring your own stack.
paragraphs.explainArabic: هذه دالة حسابية لا قياس أداء. تُظهر شكل المنحنى فقط. الأرقام الحقيقية تأتي من قياس نظامك.

prediction.question: Your retrieval budget is 4,000 tokens and a query needs 6,000. Which fix is cheapest to try first?
prediction.answer: Chunk smaller, so the retrieved set fits the budget. Changing the window size does not reduce what retrieval returned.

glossary.meaningEn: The mechanism that lets a model weigh earlier tokens when forming the current one.
glossary.meaningAr: آلية تسمح للنموذج بالترجيح بين الرموز السابقة عند تمثيل الرمز الحالي.
glossary.example: Attention is what lets a model connect bank to river.

glossary.meaningEn: A unit of text the model reads, usually a word or a word fragment.
glossary.meaningAr: وحدة نص يقرأها النموذج، غالبًا كلمة أو جزء كلمة.
glossary.example: Token counts drive cost and context limits.

glossary.meaningEn: A number that scales how much a token contributes to another.
glossary.meaningAr: عدد يحدد مدى مساهمة رمز في رمز آخر.
glossary.example: A weight of 0.4 borrows 40 percent of that token's contribution.

glossary.meaningEn: Growing with the square of the input size, so doubling the input multiplies the work by four.
glossary.meaningAr: ينمو مع مربع حجم الإدخال، فتضاعف الإدخال يربّع العمل.
glossary.example: Quadratic attention is why long contexts are expensive.

glossary.meaningEn: A slice of a document that is embedded and retrieved on its own.
glossary.meaningAr: شريحة من مستند تُضمَّن وتُسترجع بشكل مستقل.
glossary.example: Smaller chunks fit inside a smaller retrieval budget.

glossary.meaningEn: A measurement taken on real hardware, as opposed to a calculation.
glossary.meaningAr: قياس مأخوذ على عتاد حقيقي، بخلاف الحساب النظري.
glossary.example: Arithmetic shows the shape, a benchmark shows the speed.

labs.title: Attention heatmap
labs.goal: See which tokens a query attends to, and how the weights move as the sentence changes.

controls.label: Sentence
controls.default: the bank approved the river loan

controls.label: Query token
options: bank
approved
river
loan

tasks.prompt: Hover the query token 'bank' and read the weight on 'river'.
tasks.check: The river weight is high because bank and river belong to the same phrase.

tasks.prompt: Switch the query to 'approved' and compare the weight on 'river'.
tasks.check: The river weight drops because approved is about the loan, not the account.

tasks.prompt: Raise sharpness to 4.0 and look at the weight spread.
tasks.check: Weights concentrate onto the top token and the rest collapse toward zero.

labs.takeawayEn: Attention weights follow meaning, and sharper weighting concentrates the mass.
labs.takeawayAr: أوزان الانتباه تتبع المعنى، وكلما زادت الحدة تمركز التوزيع.
labs.simulationNote: Illustrative simulation, not real model output.

labs.title: Context budget planner
labs.goal: Watch retrieval cost and attention cost trade off against a fixed token budget.

tasks.prompt: Set chunk size to 400 and top-K to 4. Read the retrieved token total.
tasks.check: Retrieved tokens equal chunk size times top-K.

tasks.prompt: Raise chunk size to 800 and keep top-K at 4.
tasks.check: Retrieved tokens double and may exceed a 4,000 token budget.

tasks.prompt: Lower chunk size to 200 and raise top-K to 8.
tasks.check: Retrieved tokens stay inside the budget while coverage grows.

labs.takeawayEn: The chunk size and the number of chunks you retrieve jointly decide the context bill.
labs.takeawayAr: حجم الـ chunk وعدد القطع المسترجعة يحددان معًا فاتورة السياق.
labs.simulationNote: Illustrative simulation, not real model output.

hotspots.what: Compares the current token's query vector against every earlier key vector.
hotspots.outputs: One raw score per earlier token.
hotspots.mistakes: Treating a high score as a high probability of appearing in the answer.

hotspots.what: Turns raw scores into weights that sum to one across earlier tokens.
hotspots.mistakes: Reading a weight as a share of the final answer.

hotspots.what: Combines earlier token values into the current token's representation.
hotspots.mistakes: Forgetting that the same weights are reused by later layers.

flashcards.front: Why do chunking and retrieval exist as separate fields?
flashcards.back: Because attention cost grows quadratically with context, so you cannot keep loading everything.

quiz.prompt: A weight of 0.4 on an earlier token means what?
options: The final answer is 40 percent about that token
The current token borrows 40 percent of that token's contribution
The token appears in 40 percent of the training data
The model will output that token next
answer: The current token borrows 40 percent of that token's contribution
quiz.explanationEn: Weights scale contributions to the current representation. They are borrow shares, not answer shares.
quiz.explanationAr: الأوزان تحدد المساهمة في تمثيل الرمز الحالي، وليست نسبة من الإجابة.

quiz.prompt: Doubling the input length doubles the attention work.
options: True
False
quiz.explanationEn: Attention work grows with n squared, so doubling the input roughly quadruples it.
quiz.explanationAr: العمل ينمو مع مربع n، فتضاعف الإدخال يربّعه تقريبًا.

quiz.prompt: Put the three attention steps in the order they run.
options: Score
Weight
Mix
quiz.explanationEn: Score produces raw comparisons, weight normalizes them, mix combines the earlier tokens.

quiz.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
options: attention | a unit of text the model reads
token | the mechanism that weighs earlier tokens
benchmark | a measurement on real hardware
answer: attention | the mechanism that weighs earlier tokens
token | a unit of text the model reads
benchmark | a measurement on real hardware
quiz.explanationEn: Attention is the mechanism, token is the unit, benchmark is the measurement.
quiz.explanationAr: attention آلية، token وحدة، benchmark قياس.

quiz.prompt: Complete the function so it returns the number of token pairs.
options: return n * (n - 1) // 2
quiz.explanationEn: Each token pairs with every earlier token, so the count is n times n minus one, divided by two.
quiz.explanationAr: كل رمز يقابل كل رمز سابق، فالعدد n*(n-1)/2.

quiz.prompt: A reviewer says: 'This benchmark shows attention costs 12 million operations.' Find the problem.
options: Nothing is wrong, benchmarks are always better than arithmetic
The function computes the pair count, so it is arithmetic and not a measured benchmark
The count should be divided by two
The function ignores the model size
answer: The function computes the pair count, so it is arithmetic and not a measured benchmark
quiz.explanationEn: A formula shows the shape of the curve. Only measuring your own stack gives a real number.
quiz.explanationAr: المعادلة تُظهر الشكل فقط، والرقم الحقيقي يأتي من القياس.

quiz.prompt: In your own words, why does attention cost grow quadratically, and what engineering follows from that?
answer: Every token is compared against every earlier token
So the comparison count is n times n minus one over two
That growth means context must be managed, not maximised
quiz.answerText: Every token is compared against every earlier token, so the count of comparisons is n times n minus one over two. That is quadratic in context length. Because of it, loading everything into a long window is not affordable, so the field splits into chunking, retrieval, reranking, and caching to keep the context small.
quiz.explanationEn: Look for two parts: the n squared count, and the consequence that context must be managed rather than maximized.
quiz.explanationAr: ابحث عن جزأين: عدّ n²، وأن السياق يجب أن يُدار لا أن يُكبَّر.
